# Alerts for saved candidate searches

> **Status:** Draft
> **Agreed:** not yet
> **Roadmap:** Recruiters hear about candidates first

## Problem

Recruiters at staffing firms re-run the same five or six candidate searches every morning to see who is new. It takes about twenty minutes a day, and on busy days they skip it and a competitor reaches the candidate first.

## Outcome

A recruiter saves a search once and hears about new matches without re-running it.

**Measure:** Recruiters feel more on top of new candidates.

## Scope

**In:**

- Saving a search from the results page.
- A daily email of new matches for each saved search.

**Out:**

- SMS or push alerts.
- Sharing saved searches with teammates.

## Acceptance criteria

- **A1.** When a recruiter clicks "Save search" on a results page and enters a name, the search appears under "Saved searches" with that name.
- **A2.** Alerts for new matches should arrive in a timely manner.
- **A3.** When a saved search has no new matches since the last alert, no email is sent for it that day.
- **A4.** The alert email should be easy to scan and show the most relevant candidates appropriately.
- **A5.** When a recruiter clicks "Delete" on a saved search and confirms, it is removed from "Saved searches" and no further emails are sent for it.
- **A6.** When the recruiter saves a search with the name left blank, the form shows "Give this search a name" and nothing is saved.
